source: Wang et al. (2021/2023) PopBlends: Strategies for conceptual blending with large language models
finding: GPT-3 was used to find a connecting concept between a pop culture domain and a product, then scenes were built around it. Network types are not named in the paper.
numbers: Stage 1 (10 annotators): connecting-concept accuracy 56.0%, 55.3%, 58.7% for three GPT strategies; at least one good of five: 90.0%, 96.6%, 93.3%. Half-GPT entity attributes 57% accurate (adjectives 79%, activities 58%, catchphrases 35%).
limits: Small annotator pool; GPT-3 invents facts (catchphrases mostly wrong); no network-type analysis.
agent_relevance: Blend candidates need a fact check step. One good option out of five is common even when the average is only about 57%, so generate several and filter.

source: Wang et al. (2021/2023) PopBlends: Strategies for conceptual blending with large language models
finding: Stage 2 scene generation: product scenes relate to the connecting concept more often than retrieved pop culture scenes.
numbers: Average relatedness 89.1% product vs 75.9% pop culture (raw 80.0% vs 63.4%); at least one of two scenes related: 98.3%.
limits: 15 outputs checked.
agent_relevance: Generated material beat retrieved material for fit to the bridging idea. Use generation, then check.

source: Wang et al. (2021/2023) PopBlends: Strategies for conceptual blending with large language models
finding: User study of the blend tool against plain internet search. People produced more blend ideas, with less mental demand.
numbers: 10 students, within subjects: 2.03 (SD 0.84) vs 0.87 (SD 0.56) ideas per pair; Wilcoxon p < 0.001; all 10 said PopBlends helped more; perceived effort also lower (p = 0.006).
limits: N=10, amateur designers, pop culture only.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that supplies a bridge concept more than doubled output. Supports a shared-bridge step before blending (the generic space in Fauconnier-Turner terms).

source: Ge and Parikh (2021) Visual conceptual blending with large-scale language and vision models
finding: Split blending into reasoning (a language model finds a shared property, giving text like 'a moon sliced like an orange') and generation (an image model draws it). Language models beat ConceptNet at proposing the shared property.
numbers: Simile dataset precision P@1000: ConceptNet 37.33 in the BERT-large row, best language model 66.38. Human study on AMT: 20 descriptions, 6 questions, 9 subjects per cell; CLIP-based BigSleep and DeepDaze beat DF-GAN, BigSleep preferred over DeepDaze.
limits: Table rows are garbled in the extracted text, so the exact model-to-number pairing is uncertain. Questions map to the unpacking and integration principles, not to network types.
agent_relevance: The task is a single-property blend. Language models are better than symbolic stores at finding the shared ground. Use the model for the generic-space step.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and inducing combinational creativity in vision-language models
finding: Built a three-level frame (identify inputs, explain how combined, imply meaning) from blending theory and tested 11 VLMs on 666 artist-made mashups. Best models beat average humans, not experts.
numbers: Implication-task win rate: human experts 78.3%, GPT-4o 73.5%, GPT-4V 71.9%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 71.7%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 62.9%, average human 51.0%, Claude-3-Opus 39.2%, LLaVA-1.5-7B 20.1%. Identification precision/recall: GPT-4o 75.67/85.00; average human 53.42/70.33.
limits: Judging by GPT-4o (agreement with two human experts 85.1% and 81.6%). Images only; no named network types.
agent_relevance: Models are decent at reading the structure of a blend. Supports using a model to judge which blend type a pair needs.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and inducing combinational creativity in vision-language models
finding: Adding the explanation level (how the inputs are combined) to the generation prompt raised creative quality. The paper credits the structural guidance, not just extra detail.
numbers: Human rankings of expert vs II vs IEI images differed (p < 0.0001); IEI mean rank 1.98 vs II 2.40; Midjourney win rate vs human experts rose from 0.26 to 0.35 with IEI; all models improved. GPT-4o conceptual combination worked in 90% (36 of 40) DALLE-3 examples; 27.8% (10 of 36) good descriptions still failed to render.
limits: Image models were the bottleneck. Improvement shrank for weaker models.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that makes the model state how the two inputs combine before producing the blend gave a measurable lift. Model this as a required 'how combined' field.

source: Peng et al. (2025) Probing and inducing combinational creativity in vision-language models
finding: Two mashup kinds: fusion (traits of both objects kept) and replacement (one object stands in for another, keeping little of the second). Nine of 11 models were more precise on fusion; humans show the same pattern.
numbers: 9 of 11 models had higher precision on fusion than replacement.
limits: A visual typology, only loosely related to single-scope vs double-scope. Authors say replacement needs contextual understanding.
agent_relevance: Closest empirical hint that blends dominated by one input are harder to decode than blends keeping both. Suggestive only.

source: Xu et al. (2026) Beyond Pixels: Visual metaphor transfer via schema-driven agentic reasoning
finding: A multi-agent loop built on blending theory: one agent distills a reference into a schema (subject, carrier, relational invariant, violation, emergent meaning), one finds a new carrier while keeping the generic space fixed, one draws, one critiques and backtracks.
numbers: User-study ablation, 5-point scale (MR/MI/VA/VI/VQ): direct prompt 3.62/2.75/2.96/3.75/3.65; strong one-shot CBT prompt 3.97/3.69/3.77/3.89/4.09; no CBT description 3.88/3.66/3.68/4.04/4.12; no transfer agent 4.01/3.71/3.83/4.33/4.25; no diagnostic agent 4.26/4.05/3.98/4.61/4.48; full 4.47/4.56/4.51/4.74/4.76.
quote: Without structured guidance, the model often falls back to literal object substitution or salient-shape copying
limits: Image domain. Authors designed the metrics. Network types are not used; the loop is closest to single-scope transfer.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that a staged blend loop beats a single strong prompt, and that the critic with backtracking adds the last gain. Maps to an agent loop.

source: Xu et al. (2026) Beyond Pixels: Visual metaphor transfer via schema-driven agentic reasoning
finding: Against commercial image systems, the schema loop won most pairwise human judgments, with the largest gain on analogy appropriateness.
numbers: Judged better in 64.44% of pairs vs GPT-Image, 67.11% vs Banana-pro, 72.89% vs Midjourney, 76.22% vs BAGEL, inferior in under 10%; analogy appropriateness up 16.8% over the runner-up; aesthetic score 5.68. 100 human participants (age 14-55).
limits: Authors' own benchmark.
agent_relevance: Keeping the relational invariant fixed while swapping the surface carrier is a repeatable, checkable move.

source: Sato (2025) The Way We Prompt: Conceptual blending, neural dynamics, and prompt-induced transitions in LLMs
finding: Argues blending can be used as an experimental method on LLMs: prompts fusing distant domains can cause tone shifts (PIT) or confident but ungrounded outputs (PIH), e.g. periodic table with tarot.
numbers: No quantitative results in this review.
limits: Position paper; no controlled test; network types do not appear; neural parallels are speculative.
agent_relevance: Warning: blending distant domains is where fluent but unsupported output appears. A blend operator needs a grounding check.

source: Lynn (2026) Conceptual blending in humans and language models
finding: Single-author theory paper. Argues humans and LMs differ in source, grounding and causal closure of the control loop. Gives a toy vector-symbolic model of one blend (Osprey tiltrotor).
numbers: No experiments, no humans, no models tested; network types not mentioned.
quote: Proxy goals do not encode explanations of why a particular blend should exist or how it would work.
limits: Conceptual only; the toy code is in a supplement that was not read.
agent_relevance: A blend operator needs an explicit goal that selects what to project.

source: Lippolis et al. (2025) Meanings are like onions: a layered approach to metaphor processing
finding: Proposes a three-layer metaphor pipeline (content analysis, blending analysis, pragmatics) with a Blending Ontology that encodes four-space networks, and uses an LLM to fill it. A smoking-as-bullet example is worked through.
numbers: No benchmark numbers reported.
limits: Position paper; no evaluation.
agent_relevance: A schema (blendable, blending principle, blended) already exists as an ontology. A cheap structured output format for a blend operator.

source: Matsuhira et al. (2024) Investigating conceptual blending of a diffusion model for improving nonword-to-image generation
finding: Averaging the text embeddings of two prompts in Stable Diffusion often draws both concepts. First quantitative test of that effect.
numbers: Midpoint embedding: blended concept depicted in 62.1% (BCD 0.621), mixed concept in 86.2% (MCD 0.862); averaged over all interpolation ratios 38.9% and 47.1%. Ground-truth embeddings give blending in up to 60% of images.
limits: Image model; a symmetric mix of two words, not a chosen network type.
agent_relevance: Naive averaging gives juxtaposition or mix; a true emergent blend needs structured selection.

source: Olearo et al. (2025) Blending concepts with text-to-image diffusion models
finding: Compared four zero-shot ways to blend (textual embedding, U-Net layers, alternate prompts, switch prompts) on 22 concept pairs. No single method wins everywhere.
numbers: 100 participants ranked all four on 22 pairs. Alternate and switch tied, both preferred over UNet, and UNet over textual (p essentially 0). Alternate over switch in 51%, not significant.
limits: Results vary by category (compound words, style transfer, architecture); one concept often dominates shape or colour.
agent_relevance: Blend method should depend on the pair, which matches choosing a network type per task. One input tends to dominate unless balanced.

source: Olearo et al. (2024) How to blend concepts in diffusion models
finding: Earlier study of blending by latent-space operations. Conclusion: it works, but the best strategy depends on the context of the blend.
numbers: Not extracted in detail.
limits: Short paper.
agent_relevance: Same lesson: no universal blend operator.

source: Hernandez et al. (2024) Alien recombination: exploring concept blends beyond human cognitive availability in visual art
finding: Two GPT-2 models, one fine-tuned on art captions and one on human availability, produce concept combinations rare in art. Pushing away from what humans find available gave images rated more novel.
numbers: 85% of combinations at higher temperature had at least one new concept; GPT-4 pairwise judgments and ResNet embedding similarity both favoured the alien method.
limits: Authors note embeddings react to lighting and contrast; novel is not the same as valuable.
agent_relevance: Default model blends are the familiar ones. Forcing less available pairs raises novelty, which supports a deliberate far-pair step for double-scope style ideas.

source: Lu et al. (2025) Misty: UI prototyping through interactive conceptual blending
finding: Developers blend chosen aspects of an example UI into their own code; an LLM does the blend and shows a semantic diff to toggle.
numbers: 14 front-end developers; mean satisfaction 3.2/5 (median 3, SD 1.3) across 103 activities: 31 below 3, 44 above 3, 28 at 3; only 5 of 14 (35%) agreed it expressed their intent.
limits: Exploratory first-use study, no control.
agent_relevance: Selective projection with a diff the user can toggle is a practical control. Output often missed intent, so show what was projected.

source: Gomez-Ramirez et al. (2021) Artificial cognitively-inspired generation of the notion of topological group
finding: Formal blending (category-theory colimits, specifications in CASL) used to generate the concept of a topological group from topology and group theory.
numbers: One worked example; no numbers.
limits: Symbolic, hand-built case; no benchmark.
agent_relevance: A precedent for a checked, formal blend in math where the result can be proved.

source: Wikipedia, Conceptual blending (read 2026-11-09)
finding: Four types: simplex (one input has organising frames, the other specific elements), mirror (shared organising frame in every space), single-scope (different frames, only one projected), double-scope (different frames, parts of both projected). Notes Gibbs and Ritchie criticisms.
numbers: None.
limits: Secondary source; page gives only the monk riddle as example.
agent_relevance: Defines the choice an agent would make. The type depends on whether the two inputs share a frame.

source: Wikipedia, Conceptual blending: critics and older systems
finding: Gibbs (2000): blending is a framework, not a testable theory. Ritchie (2004): many blends can be explained by simpler integration. Older systems: Shrager (1980s), Guhe et al. (2011, basic mathematics), Lieto and Pozzato (description logic).
numbers: None.
limits: Only the summary was read, not the originals.
agent_relevance: Treat blend-type labels as a heuristic, not a validated taxonomy. Systems are covered in subfield 04.

source: arXiv search for network-type terms (run 2026-11-09)
finding: No arXiv paper uses the phrase double-scope, and the blending-LLM papers found do not manipulate simplex, mirror, single-scope or double-scope as a variable.
numbers: 'double-scope' all-field search: 0 results. 'conceptual integration' + language model: 6 results, none on blend types. 'Fauconnier Turner blending': 1 result (a 2014 physics education paper).
limits: One index only. Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs were rate-blocked and the WebSearch budget was used up, so papers outside arXiv may be missed.
agent_relevance: Evidence gap: the claim that double-scope suits novelty has no machine test that I could find. Any use in the agent is a design hypothesis.

source: Cho et al. (2025) Imagine for Me: creative conceptual blending of real images and text via blended attention (IT-Blender)
finding: A diffusion adapter that blends a real reference image with a text concept. Motivated by design fixation and the Einstellung effect. Claims to beat baselines on blending metrics and in a user study.
numbers: Specific scores not extracted this session.
limits: Only the abstract and introduction were checked in detail.
agent_relevance: Blending is used to break fixation, which the agent could also use when a first frame stalls.

source: Eppe et al. (2018) A computational framework for conceptual blending (COINVENT)
finding: Cited in Ge and Parikh as the computational framework for blending with generalisation, amalgams and consistency checks. Not opened.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Known only from a citation in an opened paper.
agent_relevance: Template for a coded blend with a consistency check.

source: Cunha et al. (2020) Let's figure this out: a roadmap for visual conceptual blending
finding: Cited by Ge and Parikh as a roadmap on visual blending. Not opened.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Reference only.
agent_relevance: Possible source of a taxonomy of visual blend types.

source: Sun et al. (2025) Creative Blends of Visual Concepts (CHI)
finding: Cited in the IT-Blender paper: a user study found that seeing blended concepts reduced cognitive load and fostered creativity. Not opened.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Second-hand claim.
agent_relevance: Supports showing the blend, not just describing it.

source: Hicke and Kristensen-McLachlan (2024) Science is exploration: computational frontiers for conceptual metaphor theory
finding: Appeared in an arXiv listing; only the title was seen.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Title only.
agent_relevance: Possible bridge to the metaphor subfield, which runs in parallel.

source: Dreyfus, Gupta and Redish (2014) Applying conceptual blending to model coordinated use of multiple ontological metaphors
finding: Uses blending to analyse how physics students combine metaphors. Only the listing was seen.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Human education study, not a machine study.
agent_relevance: Belongs to the human-side angles.
